keyframe_review.note: New keyframe; Cliopatria has no row for the Livs (its Livonian Brothers of the Sword shapes begin in 1202). The page: before the German conquests the territory was divided into 'the lands of Daugava Livonians, Satezele, Turaida, Idumeja, and Metsepole', with a second group on the northern coast of Courland (not drawn). The page gives no coordinates or area; the three circles are the researcher's reading. 1184 is the year Meinhard reached Ikšķile (Livonian Crusade page), the first dated event.

ledger.note: 1184: Meinhard reaches Ikšķile. 'Meinhard reached Ikšķile in 1184 to convert the pagan Livonians' and was consecrated Bishop of Üxküll in 1186; the Livs paid tribute to the Principality of Polotsk and were attacked by the Semigallians. The Livonians are older; 1184 is the first dated event.

ledger.note: 1198: Berthold's crusade. Berthold, a Cistercian abbot, 'arrived with a large crusader contingent in 1198', was killed in battle shortly after and his forces were defeated by Livonians (Livonians page: 'he was killed by the Livonian soldier' Ymaut; raids in 1196 and 1198).

region.text: the Daugava Livonians, round the river mouth where Riga was founded

ledger.note: 1201: Riga is founded on the Daugava Livs' land. 'Building started in 1201' on the settlement from which Riga grew; Albert made Riga the seat of his bishopric in 1201 (Livonian Crusade page).

1206: Turaida falls. 'Caupo's forces were defeated at Turaida in 1206, and the Livonians were declared converted.' Caupo stayed an ally until he was killed at the Battle of St. Matthew's Day, 21 September 1217.

region.text: Idumeja and Metsepole, the Livonian lands on the Gulf of Riga north-east of the Gauja

ledger.note: 1208: the last Livonian lands are Christian. 'In 1208, Pope Innocent III declared that all Livonians had been converted to Christianity'; the Livonians were then 'obliged to join the Knights of the Sword as infantry'. The pages give no date for Idumeja and Metsepole, so the year is the conversion's.

wars.outcome: The Livs lost the Daugava mouth (Riga, 1201), Turaida (1206) and by 1208 all their lands; Terra Mariana was established as an ecclesiastical state on 2 February 1207.
wars.note: The Livonian Crusade page dates Meinhard's mission to 1184-1186 and Berthold's to 1196-1198.

sources.note: Meinhard 1184-1186, Berthold 1198, Riga 1201, Turaida 1206, Terra Mariana 2 February 1207, Caupo killed 1217.

notes: Not a state: tribal lands and a chieftain (Caupo of Turaida). Start 1184 is the first dated event, not a founding (the Livs paid tribute to Polotsk). No capital. The Livonian Brothers of the Sword dossier files its 1202 founding at Riga and the 1206 Turaida gain as coming from 'nobody'; this dossier names those as Liv land. The Bishopric of Riga is the archbishopric-of-riga dossier (counterpart 'archbishopric-of-riga'); Terra Mariana is not a dossier. The Livonian Coast (northern Courland) Livs are not drawn: the Curonians dossier's Courland shape covers them; the pages do not say when they were conquered. The 1207 Terra Mariana establishment is dated 2 February 1207 on the Livonian Crusade page.
